summary_en: This pilot study tests histotripsy, a non-invasive procedure that uses focused ultrasound waves to break down targeted tumor tissue, added to chemoimmunotherapy in biliary tract cancer. Histotripsy is given under general anesthesia, and the chemoimmunotherapy (gemcitabine, cisplatin, and durvalumab or pembrolizumab) is given by IV infusion every 3 weeks until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The study's stated focus is safety and feasibility, and it also measures objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival, with bilirubin changes in cohort 2.
summary_es: Este estudio piloto evalúa la histotripsia, un procedimiento no invasivo que usa ondas de ultrasonido enfocadas para destruir el tejido tumoral seleccionado, añadida a la quimioinmunoterapia en el cáncer de vías biliares. La histotripsia se administra bajo anestesia general, y la quimioinmunoterapia (gemcitabina, cisplatino y durvalumab o pembrolizumab) se administra por infusión intravenosa cada 3 semanas hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o toxicidad intolerable. El enfoque declarado del estudio es la seguridad y la factibilidad, y también mide la tasa de respuesta objetiva, la duración de la respuesta, la tasa de control de la enfermedad, la supervivencia libre de progresión y la supervivencia global, con cambios en la bilirrubina en la cohorte 2.
who_for: Age 18 or older and able to give informed consent
Confirmed biliary tract cancer that is locally advanced or metastatic and not eligible for resection or transplant
No prior systemic therapy for advanced disease (recurrence after surgery must be at least 6 months after adjuvant therapy)
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and adequate blood, liver and kidney function
not_for: Prior immune-mediated therapy such as anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies
Active or prior autoimmune disorder, with listed exceptions
Uncontrolled infection, including hepatitis B, hepatitis C or uncontrolled HIV
Enrolled in another investigational trial or treated with an investigational device within 30 days of the planned procedure
